headline: NORTH ARROW DRILLS 9m AT 1.23 g/t AU AND 7m AT 1.99 g/t AU AT KRAAIPAN, BOTSWANA — 700m GOLD STRIKE CONFIRMED
snippet: North Arrow Minerals Inc. (TSXV: NAR) released Rotation 1 RC drilling assays from its US$2.3M 2026 exploration program at the Kraaipan Gold Project in southern Botswana, confirming gold mineralization along approximately 700 metres of strike at Target A — with bedrock intercepts exceeding 0.5 g/t Au in 12 of 20 holes, headlined by 9m @ 1.23 g/t Au and 7m @ 1.99 g/t Au. The project sits on the direct northern extension of the Archean greenstone terrane hosting Harmony Gold's Kalgold Mine 40km to the south, masked by shallow Kalahari sand cover. Rotation 2 drilling at Targets AE and AF (22 holes, 1,198m) is complete with results expected in 6-7 weeks.

headline: GOLD BREAKS BELOW 200-DAY EMA FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2023 — WGC BEAR SCENARIO TARGETS $3,440, A -20% SLIDE
snippet: Gold fell 1% to $4,289.87 on Monday June 8, closing below its 200-day exponential moving average for the first time since 2023 — a technically significant breach that opens the World Gold Council's bear scenario range of $3,360–$3,990 and one technical forecast pointing to $3,440 (-20% from current levels). The break compounds Friday's 3.3% drop on the May jobs shock and marks a complete erasure of 2026 year-to-date gains. However, the WGC's structural bull case — anchored by 244 tonnes of Q1 central bank buying and de-dollarisation demand — remains intact; the question is whether the technical damage attracts new trend-following sellers before the autumn seasonal catalyst.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,306 AS CPI WEEK OPENS — MAY INFLATION AT 4.2% EXPECTED, MINERS BRACED FOR BINARY VOLATILITY
snippet: FXStreet's Monday June 8 market analysis frames this week as the most important near-term pivot for gold: May CPI prints Wednesday (consensus 4.2% vs. April's 3.8%), PPI arrives Thursday, and University of Michigan inflation expectations close the week Friday. A hot CPI reading that tests $4,120–$4,138 support or breaks below $4,000 could accelerate the correction; a miss toward 3.5% could trigger a violent short-squeeze to $4,366–$4,382. Goldman Sachs maintains its $5,400 year-end target while technical signals point lower — CPI decides which camp prevails this week.

headline: GOLDSEEK JUNE 8: CENTRAL BANKS STILL BUYING AGGRESSIVELY — BUT INTRADAY TRADERS TOLD TO STAY SIDELINED UNTIL JUNE 23
snippet: GoldSeek's Asian Metals Market Update for June 8, 2026 notes that despite the sharp jobs-shock selloff, the Chinese Central Bank is 'aggressively buying physical gold and selling US bonds' as part of a broader central bank de-dollarisation trade. The analyst recommends intraday and short-term investors remain on the sidelines until June 23 — after CPI (June 10), FOMC (June 18), and University of Michigan expectations (June 12) have cleared. Copper and base metals are rated neutral-to-bullish but expected to remain volatile over the next two weeks. The Metals Focus full-year gold average forecast of $4,920/oz is cited as the structural bull floor.

headline: EXPERTS FORECAST GOLD REBOUNDS TO $4,650–$4,750 BY MONTH END — 'THIS DIP IS A STRUCTURAL ENTRY POINT'
snippet: CBS News surveyed precious metals analysts ahead of June's CPI data and found a near-consensus view that the jobs-shock selloff is temporary: Ridgemont Metals CEO Deric Ned forecasts gold in the $4,650–$4,750 range by end of month, with a base case for a $4,750 close 'once the rate-hike narrative stabilises.' Other analysts framed the move below $4,400 as a structural entry for investors with a 6-12 month horizon, noting that the forward-rate repricing removes the most dangerous speculative froth while leaving intact the central bank buying, de-dollarisation, and fiscal-deterioration drivers that built the bull market.

headline: VANECK GOLD SWOT: GOLD-SILVER RATIO FLASHES BULLISH SIGNAL AFTER JOBS-SHOCK DIVERGENCE — SILVER NOW THE LAGGARD TO BUY
snippet: VanEck's weekly Gold SWOT analysis finds the gold-silver ratio has spiked to multi-week highs after silver fell more than twice as far as gold on the May jobs shock — a divergence that historically precedes silver outperformance as the ratio mean-reverts. The report highlights that the structural silver supply deficit (projected 46.3 million ounces in 2026, the sixth consecutive year) and surging physical investment demand remain fully intact, making the paper-market selloff a potential entry point for silver exposure relative to gold miners. The Silver Institute's forecast of 227 million ounces of physical investment in 2026 — the highest since 2022 — provides the fundamental floor.

headline: GOLDSEEK ISSUE #53: GOLD STRUGGLING TO FIND A BOTTOM — WHAT THE WEEKLY MINING CHARTS ACTUALLY SHOW
snippet: GoldSeek's Issue #53 weekly mining roundup surveys the post-jobs-shock technical landscape: gold is searching for a bottom at the $4,309–$4,336 demand zone, GDXJ has held its 50-day moving average despite the paper gold selloff, and a handful of junior exploration names are bucking the tape on fresh drill results. The analyst notes a key divergence — physical buying from central banks and private investors has not followed speculative long liquidation lower, a set-up that has historically resolved upward once momentum-driven sellers exhaust.

headline: GOLDSEEK SCENARIO ANALYSIS: WHAT IF MAY CPI FALLS SIGNIFICANTLY? THE CASE FOR A VIOLENT METALS REVERSAL
snippet: GoldSeek's Asian Metals Market Update walks through the bull scenario for Wednesday's CPI: if May inflation prints at 3.5% or below — materially beneath the 4.2% consensus — the rate-hike repricing unwinds rapidly, the U.S. dollar index retraces, and gold could spike back above $4,600 in a single session as short-covering amplifies the move. Copper and silver would follow with above-average beta. The analyst argues that markets have priced in the worst-case CPI outcome and a soft print would create the most asymmetric risk/reward setup for mining equities since the March 2026 correction low.

headline: SUN SUMMIT MINERALS TURNS FIRST RIGS AT TOODOGGONE — FULLY FUNDED 10,000m PROGRAM TARGETS INAUGURAL RESOURCE
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Sun Summit Minerals
snippet: Sun Summit Minerals Corp. (TSXV: SMN) commenced its fully funded 2026 drill program at the JD Project in the Toodoggone Mining District of north-central British Columbia, with one rig operating and a second deploying imminently across the Creek Zone and Finn Zone. The 10,000-metre program is designed to investigate near-surface high-grade and bulk-tonnage gold mineralization and contribute to an inaugural NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate planned for Q1 2027. The Toodoggone district hosts several high-grade gold deposits and has attracted major-company attention as the BC Golden Triangle corridor attracts capital in the 2026 bull cycle.

headline: ATERRA METALS WRAPS TOTORA CU-AU PHASE I IN PERU — 2,746m DRILLED, FIRST ASSAYS PENDING
snippet: ATERRA Metals Inc. (CSE: ATC) completed Phase I drilling at the Totora copper-gold project, reporting 2,745.6 metres across 1,571.5m of reverse circulation and 1,174.1m of diamond drilling. All samples have been submitted to a certified laboratory with first assay results expected within weeks. Phase I tested priority structural-geological targets across the project; results will determine Phase II priorities. The Totora project is located in Peru, a top-tier copper jurisdiction, as the June 30 U.S. Commerce Department refined-copper tariff review keeps copper-project economics in sharp investor focus.

headline: ESKAY MINING RAISES $3.5M FLOW-THROUGH FOR GOLDEN TRIANGLE SUMMER DRILL PROGRAM — CLOSING JUNE 19
snippet: Eskay Mining Corp. (TSXV: ESK) announced a non-brokered flow-through private placement of up to $3.5 million at $0.48 per share, closing on or before June 19, 2026. Proceeds will fund Canadian Exploration Expenses at the company's consolidated Eskay Project in the Golden Triangle, British Columbia — a 177-claim, 52,600-hectare package 70km northwest of Stewart that sits along the Eskay rift corridor. The raise capitalises on flow-through tax incentives and keeps the summer field season funded as elevated gold prices draw capital back to BC's most prolific precious metals district.
